newsitem.title: UK: INSTANT VIEW - UK jobs, earnings, PSBR data.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - UK jobs, earnings, PSBR data.

text.p: Following is a selection of economists' reactions to UK data showing September unemployment falling 35,600 for a jobless rate of 7.4%, a September PSBR of 3.41 billion stg and August average earnings rising an underlying 4.0%.
The Reuters consensus forecast was for unemployment to fall 20,000, a PSBR of 2.7 billion stg and average earnings growth of 3.75%.
"The whole set of figures is obviously very disappointing from the markets point of view and will have a negative impact."

"That sharp fall in unemployment is going to add further to concerns that the labour market is already tight and that this could lead to some pressure on earnings. Already we see that average earnings have blipped higher and this obviously has some negative impact perhaps for inflation down the road. PSBR numbers are particularly disappointing...and give the Chancellor very little scope to cut taxes in the budget."

"It is a pretty poor combination overall, consistent with economic acceleration. The unemployment fall is certainly a lot larger than people were going for. The average earnings numbers I would treat as a surprise...I don't think there is concern yet about a trend acceleration in average earnings but clearly that remains a concern for next year. Overall, very little scope indeed for tax cuts and no case here for fiscal or monetary policy to ease."

"The UK data are stronger than expected and should underpin the rise in the GBP. Main focus will be the 4% underlying earnings growth in August - unchanged from an upward revised July increase - and surprisingly large 35.6k drop in unemployment. Both sets of data suggest that the ecomony is genuinely picking up speed, and while the reliability of the unemployment statistics is questionable, the fall is supported by a healthy 16.6k jump in vacancies. Despite the implications for stronger growth, the September PSBR was a disappointly large GBP3.4Bn despite nearly GBP1BN of privatisation proceeds."

"Data accordingly doubly negative for gilts and add to calls for a tight budget next month. GBP implications however, are favourable across the board. The report highlights the relative outperformance of the UK economy vs continental Europe and wioll add to speculation that the next move in rates is up. A hike in base rates is the last thing the government wants pre-election, so we should see an increasingly tolerant policy towards a strong/stronger pound."

"The big surprise is in the labour market figures, but a health warning should be attached that unemployment is quite volatile at this time of year with the end of temporary jobs over the summer. The underlying trend is clearly downwards, perhaps even accelerating to what we saw earlier this year. Although the fall in unemployment is probably exaggerated, the tightness in the labour market is a bit disconcerting because the average earnings figures are picking up. This is purely a pick up in cyclical earnings such as overtime, bonuses."

"This could be a portent of things to come and certainly casts doubt that cost pressures next year will be negligible, so it's all a bit worrying. The downtrend in PSBR excluding privatisation receipts is probably still intact. The Treasury is still broadly on target to hit the 27 billion stg target for the year."

"PSBR and labour market data total bad news for gilts, probably good news for sterling. Big fall in unemployment plus higher average earnings gives yet more signs that the labour market is very tight. The result will, in time be higher inflation. PSBR seems to have been biased upwards by spending effects of I-L gilt redemption."
